title: Tigon: A Distributed Database for a CXL Pod
problem: CXL-based memory pooling in data centers enables efficient resource sharing but requires distributed database designs optimized for CXL's unique latency/bandwidth characteristics and coherency model.
motivation: CXL Pods represent a new pooled memory architecture; databases must be redesigned to exploit CXL's capabilities while handling its different performance profiles compared to traditional NUMA or disaggregated architectures.
method: Tigon stores database records in a shared CXL memory pool accessible to all servers, using CXL's cache coherency feature (where all processors automatically see the same latest version of data) to maintain consistency without extra synchronization. Rather than having each server maintain its own copy and send updates across the network, Tigon optimizes data placement and update handling within the pool to take advantage of the hardware-enforced coherency. This approach reduces both access latency and the synchronization overhead of traditional distributed databases.
key_novelty: Tigon redesigns distributed database architecture to exploit CXL's shared memory pool and hardware-enforced consistency, eliminating the copying and network synchronization overhead of traditional approaches.
contributions: Database design tailored to CXL Pod architecture
Optimization of data placement and consistency for coherent shared memory
Performance tuning for CXL's latency/bandwidth characteristics
limitations: Performance gains depend on CXL pool configuration and workload access patterns; applicability to non-CXL environments unclear.
